The intake gap

Leads should not depend on memory.

The problem is rarely a lack of software. It is the handoff between website, phone, email, intake, calendar, staff and case-management tools.

01

Slow first response

New inquiries wait for a person to notice, forward or return a message.

02

Repeated data entry

The same name, matter details and contact information are typed into multiple places.

03

Missed follow-up

Reminders, callbacks and consultation follow-up depend on individual staff habits.

04

English / Spanish handoff gaps

Language changes create a second process, inconsistent wording or a manual transfer.

05

No clear lead status

Owners and intake teams cannot see what is waiting, booked, incomplete or untouched.

04 / OFFER
One workflow at a time.
Automation with boundaries

Move the work. Keep judgment human.

NBO automates repetitive administrative movement. It does not automate legal judgment or pretend an AI system should make consequential client decisions.

The system can handle

  • Immediate bilingual acknowledgment
  • Approved intake questions and data capture
  • Routing, reminders and staff alerts
  • Scheduling and follow-up sequences
  • Status visibility and exception flags

Your team keeps control of

  • Legal advice and substantive legal communication
  • Conflict review and representation decisions
  • Qualification judgment and case strategy
  • Fees, engagement and sensitive exceptions
  • Final approval of consequential communications
AI may assist selectively with drafting, classification or summarization when appropriate and approved. It is infrastructure—not the promise.
Acceptance standard: agreed workflow steps must pass documented tests before handoff. If a scoped function does not pass, NBO corrects the implementation within the agreed scope.
